name.text: Drawing a vector on a grid

questiontext.text:
The point \(A({@x0@},\,{@y0@})\) is marked on the grid. Drag the point B so that \(\overrightarrow{AB} = {@col([a,b])@}\), or type the coordinates of B in the boxes. The point and the boxes move together.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="ans1Ref" input-ref-ans2="ans2Ref" width="420px" height="420px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-6.6, 6.6, 6.6, -6.6], axis: false, grid: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); var gl = {strokeColor: '#d0d0d0', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}; for (var gx = -6; gx <= 6; gx++) { b.create('segment', [[gx, -6], [gx, 6]], gl); } for (var gy = -6; gy <= 6; gy++) { b.create('segment', [[-6, gy], [6, gy]], gl); } var tx = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 13}; var lab = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 16}; var ax = {strokeColor: '#555555', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true, highlight: false}; b.create('segment', [[-6, 0], [6, 0]], ax); b.create('segment', [[0, -6], [0, 6]], ax); for (var tk = -6; tk <= 6; tk++) { if (tk !== 0 && tk % 2 === 0) { b.create('text', [tk - 0.15, -0.45, String(tk)], tx); } } for (var tk2 = -6; tk2 <= 6; tk2++) { if (tk2 !== 0 && tk2 % 2 === 0) { b.create('text', [0.15, tk2, String(tk2)], tx); } } var A = b.create('point', [{#x0#}, {#y0#}], {name: 'A', fixed: true, size: 3, fillColor: '#000000', strokeColor: '#000000', label: {useMathJax: false, fontSize: 16, offset: [6, 10]}}); // B is dragged by the learner; it snaps to whole-number points var B = b.create('point', [-6, -6], {name: 'B', size: 5, snapToGrid: true, snapSizeX: 1, snapSizeY: 1, fillColor: '#ffffff', strokeColor: '#1f4e9c', strokeWidth: 3, label: {useMathJax: false, fontSize: 16, offset: [6, 10]}}); b.create('arrow', [A, B], {strokeColor: '#1f4e9c', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); // the point and its two number boxes move together: drag the point or type in the boxes (function (P, ex, ey) { var put = function () { ex.value = String(Math.round(P.X())); ey.value = String(Math.round(P.Y())); ex.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); ey.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); }; var get = function () { var x = parseFloat(ex.value), y = parseFloat(ey.value); if (isFinite(x) && isFinite(y)) { P.moveTo([x, y]); b.update(); } }; P.on('drag', put); P.on('up', put); ex.addEventListener('change', get); ey.addEventListener('change', get); ex.addEventListener('input', get); ey.addEventListener('input', get); get(); })(B, document.getElementById(ans1Ref), document.getElementById(ans2Ref)); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]
B = ( [[input:ans1]] , [[input:ans2]] ) [[validation:ans1]] [[validation:ans2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The column vector says how to move from A: the top number \({@a@}\) is the move across ([[if test="is(a>0)"]]right[[else]]left[[/if]]), the bottom number \({@b@}\) the move up or down ([[if test="is(b>0)"]]up[[else]]down[[/if]]).

From \(A({@x0@},\,{@y0@})\) move \({@abs(a)@}\) [[if test="is(a>0)"]]right[[else]]left[[/if]] and \({@abs(b)@}\) [[if test="is(b>0)"]]up[[else]]down[[/if]]: B is at \(({@tgt[1]@},\,{@tgt[2]@})\).

questiondescription.text:
Vectors: drawing a vector from a point

Grade 12 CBE Essential 2.2: Place the end point B of a vector AB on a grid, by dragging or by typing its coordinates, given A and the column vector.

Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: You drew the vector from the origin. \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) starts at A: move from \(A({@x0@},\,{@y0@})\).

Your arrow points the wrong way: you drew \(\overrightarrow{BA}\). From A, move \({@abs(a)@}\) [[if test="is(a>0)"]]right[[else]]left[[/if]] and \({@abs(b)@}\) [[if test="is(b>0)"]]up[[else]]down[[/if]].
You moved \({@b@}\) across and \({@a@}\) up. The top number is the move across.
One of your moves goes the wrong way. A positive number means right or up, a negative number left or down.

falsefeedback.text: Your B is at \(({@ans1@},\,{@ans2@})\), so your arrow from A is the vector \({@col(zV)@}\), not \({@col([a,b])@}\). From A, move \({@a@}\) across and \({@b@}\) up (a negative number means left or down). B goes there.
